method: Source-gated qualitative ordering by bottleneck specificity, plausible technical path, horizon tractability, potential impact, independent verification feasibility, and counterevidence. No numerical weights, probabilities, or attention proxies.

screening_scope.why_no_new_events_frozen: New leads either overlap an existing research family or lack a non-arbitrary, comparable, independently adjudicable threshold. The final portfolio is a qualitative snapshot, not silently inserted into the frozen-event registry.

2027-2028.research_question: Can automated systems build coherent implementations and machine-checked proofs across multi-module repositories with cross-module invariants, rather than only solve isolated obligations?
2027-2028.subfield: formal verification; software engineering; AI systems
2027-2028.anticipated_breakthrough: Further independently checked gains in repository-level code-and-proof task completion and success-cost trade-offs on version-frozen tasks; not general autonomous software engineering.
2027-2028.progress_direction: incremental algorithmic and empirical progress is qualitatively favored over full general resolution
2027-2028.strongest_baseline: Vero reports 27/43 code-and-proof full solves for its strongest tested configuration and 10 instances resistant to all evaluated configurations; VeriSoftBench reports dependency-closure difficulty; CoCo-Prover reports up to 26/43 Vero solves and lower cost in selected matched settings.

supporting_evidence.claim: Vero has 43 repository instances; the source reports 27/43 full code-and-proof solves by the strongest evaluated configuration.
VeriSoftBench contains 500 repository-context Lean obligations and reports multi-hop dependency difficulty.
CoCo-Prover reports up to 26/43 solves on Vero; author-reported, not independently replicated here.

2027-2028.main_obstacle: Cross-module invariants, reusable lemma libraries, specification fidelity, full repository buildability, and cost-controlled evaluation.
2027-2028.strongest_counterevidence: Finite curated benchmark, rapid model changes, author-run comparisons, and proof correctness only relative to formalized specifications.
2027-2028.potential_impact: High if formal specifications correspond to intended behavior and the result transfers to held-out repositories.
2027-2028.source_confidence: High for existence and reported benchmark numbers; moderate for cross-paper comparability; no independent replication in this project.
2027-2028.what_changes_ranking: Independent rerun with frozen versions, equal budgets, held-out repositories, kernel-checked proofs, clean builds, and external specification audit.
2027-2028.independent_verification: Repeat on fixed repository commits; publish task-level outcomes, budget, proof-check logs, build results, hidden tests, and independent spec review.
2027-2028.paper4_next_evidence_action: Document benchmark version, solved-instance overlap, cost model, and proof/spec audit for Vero and CoCo before any authorized new evaluation.

2027-2028.research_question: Can serving systems jointly schedule speculative execution, KV-cache residency, and requests under changing arrivals to improve goodput or tail latency at fixed output quality, memory, and SLO?
2027-2028.anticipated_breakthrough: Configuration-specific, reproducible gains from integrated inference scheduling under explicit quality/memory/tail-latency constraints.
2027-2028.progress_direction: measurable systems improvement more plausible than a universal online-competitive theorem
2027-2028.strongest_baseline: KV-constrained online scheduling has model-specific stochastic/semi-online guarantees and a fully adversarial impossibility; Spexis reports up to 34% higher request rate over its selected best TP/PP baseline across GPU configurations.

supporting_evidence.claim: The paper distinguishes semi-online, stochastic-arrival, and fully adversarial settings and proves no constant competitive ratio in the latter model.
Spexis reports up to 34% higher request rate in an evaluated configuration and provides code; no independent reproduction here.
A heterogeneous-memory KV placement model derives an upper bound/headroom rather than a complete runtime policy.

2027-2028.main_obstacle: Composing cache residency, speculation acceptance, preemption, arrival skew, quality preservation, and tail-SLO constraints.
2027-2028.strongest_counterevidence: Adversarial online impossibility and configuration-specific speedups that may vanish under equal memory, quality, or realistic load.
2027-2028.potential_impact: High for inference latency, throughput, energy, and serving cost.
2027-2028.source_confidence: High for source-reported methods/results; moderate for external generalization.
2027-2028.what_changes_ranking: Independent equal-memory/equal-quality trace replay with p95/p99 and energy measurements.
2027-2028.independent_verification: Version-lock models, hardware, traces and kernels; compare against best tuned baselines with identical memory and output quality.
2027-2028.paper4_next_evidence_action: Audit Spexis evaluation conditions and baselines against common serving traces; no run was authorized or performed.

2027-2028.research_question: Can fully adaptive privacy filters for subsampled Gaussian mechanisms obtain sound and useful approximation guarantees in the intermediate sampling-rate regime, under explicit adaptivity and parameter assumptions?
2027-2028.anticipated_breakthrough: A theorem or impossibility boundary for a restricted intermediate-rate family, potentially with certified approximation error.
2027-2028.progress_direction: restricted theorem or sharpened boundary more plausible than a universally tight filter
2027-2028.strongest_baseline: Tran et al. refute the naive f-DP filter, characterize validity conditions, and construct approximate GDP filters for q<0.2 and q>0.8 under stated asymptotic assumptions.

supporting_evidence.claim: The primary paper proves the naive fully adaptive construction invalid and presents approximate filters in low/high q regimes.

2027-2028.main_obstacle: Full adaptivity and rigorous error/tightness control for intermediate q; comparator must be specified consistently.
2027-2028.strongest_counterevidence: The gap may resist useful approximation or existing RDP/PLD accounting may dominate for target applications.
2027-2028.potential_impact: High for privacy/utility trade-offs if guarantees are sound and operational.
2027-2028.source_confidence: High for the theorem statements; medium for interpreting the full uncovered parameter domain without a separate theorem review.
2027-2028.what_changes_ranking: A rigorous mid-regime theorem, lower bound, or proof that the frozen comparator already subsumes the proposed improvement.
2027-2028.independent_verification: Two theorem reviewers check quantifiers; certified arithmetic checks numerical claims separately.
2027-2028.paper4_next_evidence_action: Map the exact primary-source assumptions and frozen RDP comparator before proposing an experiment.
2027-2028.frozen_record_caveat: Original event retained unchanged; comparator and strict-improvement region are flagged as underspecified in the technical audit.

2027-2028.research_question: Can general-graph fully dynamic (1-epsilon)-approximate maximum matching achieve O(n^(1-delta)) amortized update time for fixed positive constants under the exact frozen output and adversary model?
2027-2028.anticipated_breakthrough: A theorem-level exponent improvement or a new compatible extremal bound narrowing the update-time gap.
2027-2028.progress_direction: partial bound improvement is more plausible than full resolution of the ORS extremal bottleneck
2027-2028.strongest_baseline: Approximate matching bounds connect to ordered Ruzsa-Szemeredi structure; 2025 sublinear dynamic maximal matching is adjacent but not the same objective.

supporting_evidence.claim: Primary source derives dynamic approximate-matching bounds through ordered RS graphs and leaves an extremal parameter gap.
Bernstein et al. give sublinear update time for maximal matching; this does not prove approximate maximum matching.

2027-2028.main_obstacle: The ordered RS parameter and exponent loss in its reduction to dynamic approximate maximum matching.
2027-2028.strongest_counterevidence: The key extremal question has remained difficult; results for maximal matching or another adversary do not transfer.
2027-2028.potential_impact: High for dynamic graph data structures and graph analytics.
2027-2028.source_confidence: High for the problem distinction and published result; moderate for expected transfer of new extremal progress.
2027-2028.what_changes_ranking: A new ORS result with a fully checked parameter-preserving reduction, or a barrier ruling out the frozen exponent target.
2027-2028.independent_verification: Check theorem model, amortization, adversary, output representation, preprocessing and the full reduction.
2027-2028.paper4_next_evidence_action: Trace theorem-level descendants of the ORS construction and quantify exponent implications before action selection.
2027-2028.related_event_caveat: Same research family; ORS record contains a 2030/2031 deadline conflict and is not independently adjudicable as written.

2027-2028.research_question: Can verifier signals predict independently checked final-artifact correctness and improve end-to-end multi-agent task success after false positives, false negatives, and cost are counted?
2027-2028.anticipated_breakthrough: A task-conditional verifier or clear negative theorem/evaluation showing when process supervision helps or fails.
2027-2028.progress_direction: evaluation and restricted verifier improvements more plausible than universal process verification
2027-2028.strongest_baseline: MAS-ProVe evaluates three verification paradigms, multiple granularities, verifiers, contexts, and agent frameworks; reports inconsistent gains and high variance.

supporting_evidence.claim: Published preprint reports process verification does not consistently improve multi-agent performance and often has high variance.

2027-2028.main_obstacle: Obtaining independent artifact-level labels without shared judge/model errors or benchmark leakage.
2027-2028.strongest_counterevidence: Verifier accuracy may not translate into improved task success after compute/context overhead; partial trajectories may be intrinsically ambiguous.
2027-2028.potential_impact: High if it prevents harmful or incorrect agent actions; unproven in deployed workflows.
2027-2028.source_confidence: High for the reported study scope; moderate for cross-task implications.
2027-2028.what_changes_ranking: Prospective paired artifact outcomes with independent review and net-cost gains across task families.
2027-2028.independent_verification: Freeze verifier outputs before tests; check artifacts with deterministic tests/formal proofs or independent human adjudication.
2027-2028.paper4_next_evidence_action: Inspect MAS-ProVe error strata and contrast trajectory-level signals with repository-level artifact checks.

2029-2031.research_question: Does the ordered Ruzsa-Szemeredi parameter at fixed linear matching density admit polynomial growth strong enough, through a parameter-preserving reduction, to yield fixed-exponent sublinear update time for approximate dynamic maximum matching?
2029-2031.anticipated_breakthrough: A stronger extremal bound or matching-update theorem that narrows the ORS-to-update-time gap; full polynomial ORS resolution remains uncertain.
2029-2031.progress_direction: theorem-level partial progress qualitatively favored over complete closure
2029-2031.strongest_baseline: Assadi, Khanna and Kiss connect dynamic matching update bounds to ordered RS graphs; the frozen target specifies a polynomial lower bound needed for fixed exponent.

supporting_evidence.claim: The primary source develops the ordered-RS connection and states the extremal gap.

2029-2031.main_obstacle: Extremal growth and the precise exponent transfer under every reduction parameter.
2029-2031.strongest_counterevidence: The extremal parameter may be resistant to polynomial lower bounds; adjacent maximal-matching work does not transfer.
2029-2031.potential_impact: High in dynamic graph algorithms; independent of practical deployment prevalence.
2029-2031.source_confidence: High for the published connection; forecast path remains speculative.
2029-2031.what_changes_ranking: A parameter-preserving theorem, a new obstruction, or a compatible reduction from a solved extremal conjecture.
2029-2031.independent_verification: Independent proof audit of extremal statement and reduction; keep ORS and matching as one dependent family.
2029-2031.paper4_next_evidence_action: Search exact theorem citations and inspect exponent losses; no numeric information gain is assigned.
2029-2031.related_event_caveat: ORS deadline conflict is preserved; this qualitative family forecast does not resolve that frozen defect.

2029-2031.research_question: Is exact unweighted planar Three-Sets Cut-Uncut polynomial-time solvable when two terminal sets are singletons and a third set has two terminals that must remain connected?
2029-2031.anticipated_breakthrough: An exact polynomial-time algorithm or a matching structural complexity barrier for the explicitly frozen (1,1,2) case.
2029-2031.progress_direction: substantive theorem progress plausible; exact resolution uncertain
2029-2031.strongest_baseline: Bentert et al. solve planar Two-Sets Cut-Uncut in randomized FPT time in terminal count and explicitly pose the specified Three-Sets case as open.

supporting_evidence.claim: Primary proceedings paper states adjacent theorem and open (1,1,2) case.

2029-2031.main_obstacle: Maintaining connectivity of the two-vertex terminal set while separating the three terminal sets.
2029-2031.strongest_counterevidence: The uncut constraint is precisely what ordinary multiway-cut algorithms omit; related unrestricted variants are hard.
2029-2031.potential_impact: Moderate-to-high algorithmic value for planar cut problems and structural methods.
2029-2031.source_confidence: High for the explicit primary-source open question; current later-work coverage is not exhaustive.
2029-2031.what_changes_ranking: A later source directly addresses the case, or a hardness result matching the exact planar unweighted setting.
2029-2031.independent_verification: Compare all terminal, connectivity, exactness and runtime quantifiers against primary theorem and proof.
2029-2031.paper4_next_evidence_action: Check citation descendants of the ICALP paper and equivalent formulations preserving the uncut pair.

2029-2031.research_question: Can exact discrete Fréchet distance under arbitrary translation for two planar n-vertex curves be computed in O(n^4 log^C n) time under a model comparable to the known result?
2029-2031.anticipated_breakthrough: A comparable-model algorithm reaching the frozen n^4 polylog target, or a theorem clarifying that the conditional barrier rules out the intended improvement.
2029-2031.progress_direction: model/theorem clarification more plausible than large exponent improvement
2029-2031.strongest_baseline: Bringmann, Künnemann and Nusser report an approximately n^(14/3) upper bound and a SETH-based n^(4-o(1)) lower bound for the target problem.

supporting_evidence.claim: Primary source gives the upper/lower-bound neighborhood and translation problem scope.

2029-2031.main_obstacle: Conditional lower bound is close to n^4; exact value, decision reduction, arithmetic and bit complexity must align.
2029-2031.strongest_counterevidence: The remaining asymptotic room is narrow and could be only logarithmic/model-level.
2029-2031.potential_impact: Moderate theoretical impact; specialized but foundational geometry primitive.
2029-2031.source_confidence: High for the historical source bounds; later theorem-level search remains finite and non-exhaustive.
2029-2031.what_changes_ranking: A direct comparable-model theorem or a sharper conditional lower bound.
2029-2031.independent_verification: Audit exact input representation, arithmetic operations, exact-value reduction, and SETH assumption.
2029-2031.paper4_next_evidence_action: Check later citation chain for a target-matching theorem; do not count 1D/continuous variants.

2029-2031.research_question: Does exact optimization for the frozen two-stage integer-program class remain fixed-parameter tractable when local dimensions/coefficients are parameter-bounded but global coupling matrices are unrestricted?
2029-2031.anticipated_breakthrough: An exact parameterized algorithm or a hardness boundary clarifying the role of large global entries.
2029-2031.progress_direction: narrow theorem or obstruction plausible; broad optimization claim uncertain
2029-2031.strongest_baseline: Cslovjecsek et al. prove related two-stage feasibility and uniform n-fold optimization results, not the frozen unrestricted-global-matrix optimization target.

supporting_evidence.claim: Primary article distinguishes the known structured classes and parameterization.

2029-2031.main_obstacle: Global coefficient magnitude may encode complexity not controlled by the local parameters.
2029-2031.strongest_counterevidence: Neighboring feasibility results do not entail optimization; unbounded coefficients can break the proposed tractability route.
2029-2031.potential_impact: High for structured optimization if global blocks can be handled without parameter blow-up.
2029-2031.source_confidence: High for the distinction from adjacent results; source-level exact frozen model merits specialist review.
2029-2031.what_changes_ranking: A theorem/hardness result under the exact matrix encoding, objective and parameter tuple.
2029-2031.independent_verification: Match variable domains, objective, feasibility/unboundedness handling, bit complexity, and parameter dependence.
2029-2031.paper4_next_evidence_action: Compare the two-stage theorem and n-fold optimization theorem in the full primary paper; do not infer transfer.

2029-2031.research_question: Can a research agent generate a frozen falsifiable question, execute a discriminating study, preserve auditable raw artifacts, and obtain independent reproduction more reliably than simple baselines?
2029-2031.subfield: AI for science; empirical research methods
2029-2031.anticipated_breakthrough: A reliable end-to-end evaluation protocol and narrow agent capability for reproducible evidence production, rather than general autonomous discovery.
2029-2031.progress_direction: benchmark/protocol progress likely; independent discovery capability remains very uncertain
2029-2031.strongest_baseline: EIG and ResearchBench measure proposal/inspiration metrics; PaperBench measures replication; Mao's astronomy backtesting provides prospective outcome protocol but reports low human taxonomy agreement (kappa 0.17 in its study). These are different outcomes.

supporting_evidence.claim: EIG reports proposal-native ideation metric gains, not executed scientific findings.
ResearchBench evaluates inspiration retrieval, hypothesis composition, and ranking.
PaperBench evaluates replication of 20 AI papers with decomposed rubrics.
Historical backtesting reports a 200-question prospective astronomy instance and low human outcome-label agreement in a study.

2029-2031.main_obstacle: Outcome taxonomy reliability, novelty adjudication, execution provenance, and independent reproduction across domains.
2029-2031.strongest_counterevidence: Current benchmarks divide ideation, replication, and truth verification; no source establishes a general executed-science agent capability.
2029-2031.potential_impact: Potentially transformative, but impact is conditional on correctness and reproducibility rather than proposal quality.
2029-2031.source_confidence: High that the cited benchmarks differ; low for the forecast that they will converge into a dependable system.
2029-2031.what_changes_ranking: A prospective study with reliable human labels and independently reproduced findings, or evidence that label agreement remains inadequate.
2029-2031.independent_verification: Blinded independent reviewers assess question novelty and outcomes; reproduce code/data/results; report agreement and missingness.
2029-2031.paper4_next_evidence_action: Compare endpoint and adjudicator reliability across EIG, ResearchBench, PaperBench, and astronomy backtesting.
